_: Hand-written prose for the roadmap's request-driven entries. NOT a list of what is
on the page — the issue tracker is that, and this file cannot add or remove an entry.
WHAT DECIDES WHETHER SOMETHING APPEARS, and where:
enhancement + accepted    -> 'From your requests'. I am going to build this.
enhancement + considered  -> 'Later / maybe'. Interesting, not committed.
bug + accepted            -> 'Known bugs' (see bugs.json).
no `accepted` / `considered`  -> nowhere. Filing publishes nothing.
closed                    -> nowhere, immediately. Shipping or refusing a thing and
closing its issue is the only bookkeeping there is.
Labels, in other words — not this file. Applying one needs Triage, so the gate is
closed to the people who file and open to me, which is the point: the roadmap is a
published page and everything on it is something I am asserting.
Promotion is a label edit: `considered` -> `accepted` moves an entry from Later /
maybe into its own card, and nothing here changes.
overrides — keyed by issue number as a string. A generated entry is a starting
point, not a verdict: whatever is here wins over what the reporter
wrote. The issue decides THAT it appears; this decides how it reads.
title      replace the heading
railLabel  shorter label for the contents rail
html       replace the body outright, as lines of HTML. Once set, the
reporter's prose is no longer rendered — carry over
anything that mattered.
note       append one paragraph, keeping the reporter's prose
near       the § section it sits beside
A § number is a POSITION in the backlog and moves whenever I reorder it, so any
§n written here — in `near`, or in `html` prose — is a thing that can go stale in
a commit that never touched this file. Always pair one with its anchor
(`§5`); the anchor is a content slug and does not move,
and `roadmap-data.mjs --check` will not catch a number that is merely wrong.
credit     GitHub handle to thank. Asked-for, not written-by.
hide       true to keep the label and stay off the page
Refusing something is not recorded here and never appears: close it, and if the
reason is a boundary worth writing down it earns a card in 'Considered and set
aside' in roadmap.html by hand. A no should cost me a sentence.
Render with `node scripts/roadmap-data.mjs`.

7.title: Richer author portraits
html: Resolve the author's Wikidata entry via the book, so a photo appears even
when the Open Library record is sparse. The disambiguation already picks the right
person; this only widens coverage, which is why it is small enough to say yes to.
It should land after §9, not before: once sources
are mine to pick, looking a person up should query Wikidata and not waste a call on
TMDB. Doing it in the other order would bake in the fan-out that section exists to end.

12.title: Audio review, in the browser only
html: Reading a due card aloud, using the browser's own SpeechSynthesis. It
costs the server nothing, needs no key, and works offline once <a
href="#mobile-pwa">§5's service worker
exists — which is the entire reason this can be accepted while server-side speech
stays refused. Those are not the same feature wearing different clothes: one is a
model and an audio pipeline on a box that cannot spare either, and the other is an
API the browser already ships.
Accepted rather than parked because the line it sat next to turned out to be drawn
in the right place already — see
OCR, and speech, on the server. Scope: a play control on a
review card and nothing else. No stored audio, no transcription, no server route.

2.title: AI summaries (opt-in)
html: A passive digest: batch recent highlights and summarise them with an
OpenAI-compatible model — local or remote, your endpoint, your key.
Grouped by book, tag or whole library; weekly or on-demand. Off unless configured,
generated async, and — true to the frugality goal — no cron dependency.
The digest has to be worth opening in the app on its own before any question of pushing
it arises, which is why delivery is the separate entry below and neither one waits on
the other.

3.title: Notifications (opt-in)
html: Would start with NTFY, likely routed through a multi-service notifier such as <a
href="https://containrrr.dev/shoutrrr/">Shoutrrr so one config reaches any backend —
the email digest fallback below is that same slot with a different
transport. Non-negotiable, whatever I pick: <strong>high / urgent priority must carry
through — a resurfaced highlight is a gentle nudge, but "lookup is failing"
should be able to shout, and that case alone justifies this even if no summary ever gets

generated.
This sat in the numbered backlog until I moved it here deliberately,
because anything that pushes needs something that wakes up on its own. The cheap end of
the ask needs none of it: the app-icon badge already shipped and shows a due-card
count with no server work and nothing scheduled.

4.title: Anki export / import
html: — bridge the daily review to and from Anki decks (.apkg), a natural pairing
for the spaced-repetition audience. Still being scoped; I need to learn the format
first.

5.title: Backlinks & freeform notes
html: — manually-maintained links between related highlights, Zettelkasten-style, and
standalone notes not tied to any book. Kept deliberately manual; no auto-suggested
"related" magic.

6.title: Shared / household libraries
html: — collaborative or shared-view libraries across the users on one box.

8.title: Email digest fallback
html: (SMTP) — the same delivery slot as the notifier above, for people who would rather not
run one.

9.title: Semantic search
html: (sqlite-vec) — a dependency, an indexing pass and a model, on a box budgeted
at 20–40 MB RSS. Deferred indefinitely rather than left unsaid: the two read the same
from outside and only one of them is honest.

10.title: Summary export
html: to Markdown / Obsidian.

11.title: Reviving a rating
html: The 1–5 stars were retired on purpose in 0.4.3 and ♥ is the cleaner
signal, so this is recorded as a reversal to weigh rather than as planned work — but
half-stars are the single most-cited feature of the trackers people arrive from, and the
columns are still there, inert, from before the drop. If it ever comes back it should be
per-user and opt-in, so the default library looks exactly as it does now.

13.title: A voice note on a quote
html: — record, store, play back, with no transcription, which would be a dependency. For the
reaction you can't type while reading.
